{{one source|date=December 2023}}
{{Short description|Invariant for finitely generated modules over a Noetherian ring}}
In [[commutative algebra|commutative]] and [[homological algebra|homological]] algebra, the '''grade''' of a [[finitely generated module|finitely generated]] [[Module (mathematics)|module]] <math>M</math> over a [[Noetherian ring]] <math>R</math> is a [[cohomology|cohomological]] invariant defined by vanishing of [[Ext functor|Ext-modules]]<ref name=Matsumura1>{{cite book |last=Matsumura |first=Hideyuki |author-link=Hideyuki Matsumura |date=1987 |title=Commutative Ring Theory |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/commutative-ring-theory/02819830750568B06C16E6199F3562C1 |location=Cambridge |publisher=Cambridge University Press | page=131 |isbn=9781139171762}}</ref>

<math>\textrm{grade}\,M=\textrm{grade}_R\,M=\inf\left\{i\in\mathbb{N}_0:\textrm{Ext}_R^i(M,R)\neq 0\right\}.</math>

For an [[ideal (ring theory)|ideal]] <math>I\triangleleft R</math> the grade is defined via the [[quotient ring]] viewed as a module over <math>R</math>

<math>\textrm{grade}\,I=\textrm{grade}_R\,I=\textrm{grade}_R\,R/I=\inf\left\{i\in\mathbb{N}_0:\textrm{Ext}_R^i(R/I,R)\neq 0\right\}.</math>

The grade is used to define [[perfect ideal]]s. In general we have the inequality

<math>\textrm{grade}_R\,I\leq\textrm{proj}\dim(R/I)</math>

where the [[projective dimension]] is another cohomological invariant.

The grade is tightly related to the [[Depth (ring theory)|depth]], since

<math>\textrm{grade}_R\,I=\textrm{depth}_{I}(R).</math>

Under the same conditions on <math>R, I</math> and <math>M</math> as above, one also defines the <math>M</math>-grade of <math>I</math> as<ref name=BrodmannSharpe1>{{cite book |last1=Brodmann |first1=Markus P. |last2=Sharp |first2=Rodney Y. |date=2013 |title=Local Cohomology |edition=2nd |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/local-cohomology/38D0015D6B6908D9CB9792A6276B9E60 |location=Cambridge |publisher=Cambridge University Press | page=113 |isbn=
    9780511629204}}</ref>

<math>\textrm{grade}_M\,I=\inf\left\{i\in\mathbb{N}_0:\textrm{Ext}_R^i(R/I,M)\neq 0\right\}.</math>

This notion is tied to the existence of maximal [[Regular sequence|<math>M</math>-sequences]] contained in <math>I</math> of length <math>\textrm{grade}_M\,I</math>.
